# A realistic merge: both branches edit the same secret in disjoint regions AND
# one branch adds a user. The secret driver merges the content, the audit-log
# driver merges the membership change, and the result verifies.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

cp base.txt $TMPDIR/base.txt
cp ours.txt $TMPDIR/ours.txt
cp theirs.txt $TMPDIR/theirs.txt

exec sesam init --user admin --install-merge
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

# Base secret, shared by both branches.
cp $TMPDIR/base.txt secret.txt
exec sesam add secret.txt --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add secret'

# OURS: edit the first line of the secret and add bob.
exec git checkout -b ours
cp $TMPDIR/ours.txt secret.txt
exec sesam seal
exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours: edit + add bob'

# THEIRS: edit the last line of the secret only.
exec git checkout -b theirs ours~1
cp $TMPDIR/theirs.txt secret.txt
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'theirs: edit last line'

# Merge: the secret driver merges the content cleanly; the log driver merges the
# membership change but reports a conflict (exit 1) so git stops before commit.
exec git checkout ours
! exec git merge theirs
stdout 'merged it automatically'

# The revealed plaintext holds both disjoint edits, no conflict markers.
grep 'first = OURS' secret.txt
grep 'last = THEIRS' secret.txt
grep 'middle = BASE' secret.txt
! grep '^<<<<<<< ' secret.txt

# The merged log verifies and records bob's tell plus the merge entry.
exec sesam verify --verify-mode no-disk
exec sesam show .sesam/audit/log.jsonl
stdout '"user": "bob"'
stdout '"operation": "merge"'

-- base.txt --
first = BASE
middle = BASE
last = BASE

-- ours.txt --
first = OURS
middle = BASE
last = BASE

-- theirs.txt --
first = BASE
middle = BASE
last = THEIRS
